count-120-skill-01.target: I can count a group of objects and write the number.

remedial.prompt: How many counters are in the ten frame?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 8 red counters.

steps: Touch each counter as you count.

standard.prompt: Count the counters. How many are there?

spec.alt: Ten frames with 17 red counters.

steps: Count the counters. A full ten frame has 10.

count-120-skill-01.misconception: Skipping or double-counting objects that are not in a line.
count-120-skill-01.howToAddress: Touch and move each object as it is counted, or count objects in ten frames.
commonErrors: switched the tens and the ones

count-120-skill-02.target: I can count forward from any number up to 120 and say what number comes next.

remedial.prompt: What number is hidden by the question mark?

spec.alt: Part of a number chart from 1 to 20. One box shows a question mark.

steps: Look at the numbers on each side and above or below.

standard.prompt: Which number belongs in the box with the question mark?

spec.alt: Part of a number chart from 51 to 70. One box shows a question mark.

steps: Look at the numbers on each side and above or below.

count-120-skill-02.misconception: Getting stuck at a decade change (…48, 49, 40) or after 100 (…109, 200).
count-120-skill-02.howToAddress: Use a 120 chart: when the ones reach 9, move to the next row and the tens go up by one.

count-120-skill-03.target: I can read and write numbers to 120 and match number words to numerals.

remedial.prompt: What number is shown by the tens and ones?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 1 ten rods and 7 ones cubes.

standard.prompt: Write the number shown by the blocks.

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 7 tens rods and 2 ones cubes.

count-120-skill-03.misconception: Writing numbers as they sound (one hundred four → 1004) or reversing teen digits (sixteen → 61).
count-120-skill-03.howToAddress: Build the number with tens and ones, then write the tens digit first.
commonErrors: switched the tens and the ones
wrote each part as it sounds

count-120-skill-04.skill: Counting On and Back to Add and Subtract
count-120-skill-04.target: I can count on to add and count back to subtract.

remedial.prompt: Start at 4 on the number line. Count back 2. Where is the landing point?

spec.alt: Number line from 0 to 15. A point is marked at 4.

steps: Make 2 jumps to the left from 4.

standard.prompt: Start at 11 on the number line. Count on 3. Where is the landing point?

spec.alt: Number line from 5 to 25. A point is marked at 11.

steps: Make 3 jumps to the right from 11.

count-120-skill-04.misconception: Counting the start number as the first jump (5 + 3 → 5, 6, 7).
count-120-skill-04.howToAddress: Say the start number, then count only the jumps on a number line.
commonErrors: counted the start number as a jump

add-subtract-10-skill-01.target: I can add two numbers with a sum up to 10.

remedial.prompt: Red and yellow counters are in the ten frame. How many in all?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 2 red counters and 3 yellow counters.

steps: There are 2 red and 3 yellow counters.

standard.prompt: Red and yellow counters are in the ten frame. How many in all?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 5 red counters and 5 yellow counters.

steps: There are 5 red and 5 yellow counters.

add-subtract-10-skill-01.misconception: Counting all objects again instead of counting on, and losing track.
add-subtract-10-skill-01.howToAddress: Put the bigger number in your head and count on the smaller number.
commonErrors: counted on and included the first number

remedial.prompt: The crossed out counters are taken away. How many are left?

spec.alt: 6 counters. 2 of them are crossed out.

steps: There are 6 counters and 2 are crossed out.

standard.prompt: Some counters are crossed out. How many are left?

spec.alt: 5 counters. 1 of them are crossed out.

steps: There are 5 counters and 1 are crossed out.

add-subtract-10-skill-02.misconception: Subtracting the larger number from the smaller one, or adding instead of taking away.
add-subtract-10-skill-02.howToAddress: Act it out with counters: show the whole, take some away, count what is left.
commonErrors: counted back and included the starting number

add-subtract-10-skill-03.target: I can find the number that goes with another number to make 10.

remedial.prompt: How many more counters are needed to fill the ten frame?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 8 counters and 2 empty boxes.

standard.prompt: How many empty boxes are in the ten frame?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 2 counters and 8 empty boxes.

add-subtract-10-skill-03.misconception: Thinking 6 and 3 make ten because the ten frame looks almost full.
add-subtract-10-skill-03.howToAddress: Fill a ten frame and count the empty boxes.

add-subtract-10-skill-04.target: I can break a number up to 10 into two parts and find a missing part.

remedial.prompt: The ten frame shows 5. How many yellow counters are there?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 3 red counters and 2 yellow counters.

standard.prompt: The ten frame shows 8. How many yellow counters are there?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 5 red counters and 3 yellow counters.

add-subtract-10-skill-04.misconception: Adding the whole and the part instead of finding the missing part.
add-subtract-10-skill-04.howToAddress: Use a part-part-whole mat: cover one part and ask what is hiding.

add-subtract-20-skill-01.target: I can add within 20 by making a ten, using doubles, or counting on.

remedial.prompt: Red and yellow counters fill the ten frames. How many in all?

spec.alt: Two ten frames with 1 red counter and 10 yellow counters.

steps: 1 red and 10 yellow. Fill the first ten frame, then count the rest.

standard.prompt: Find the total number of counters.

spec.alt: Two ten frames with 3 red counters and 8 yellow counters.

steps: 3 red and 8 yellow. Fill the first ten frame, then count the rest.

add-subtract-20-skill-01.misconception: Counting on from the smaller number and losing count, or forgetting part of the second number after making ten.
add-subtract-20-skill-01.howToAddress: Fill a ten frame first, then add the leftover counters in a second frame.
commonErrors: counted on and included the first number

add-subtract-20-skill-02.target: I can subtract within 20 by counting back, going back to 10, or thinking addition.

remedial.prompt: Use the number line. Start at 16. Jump back 2. Where is the end point?

spec.alt: Number line from 0 to 20.

standard.prompt: Use the number line. Start at 15. Jump back 9. Where is the end point?

spec.alt: Number line from 0 to 20.

steps: Jump back 5 to get to 10, then the rest.

add-subtract-20-skill-02.misconception: Subtracting the smaller ones digit from the larger one (14 − 6 → 12).
add-subtract-20-skill-02.howToAddress: Ask “6 plus what makes 14?” and jump to 10 first on a number line.
commonErrors: counted back and included the starting number
forgot to go back past ten

add-subtract-20-skill-03.skill: Adding in Any Order and Adding Three Numbers
add-subtract-20-skill-03.target: I can change the order of addends and add three numbers by finding a ten first.

remedial.prompt: Add the last two numbers first. What number makes this true? 3 + 7 + 3 = 3 + ___

standard.prompt: 8 + 3 = 11. Fill in the blank: 8 + 3 = 3 + ___
steps: Changing the order of the addends does not change the sum.

add-subtract-20-skill-03.misconception: Thinking 3 + 8 and 8 + 3 have different answers, or leaving out one of three addends.
add-subtract-20-skill-03.howToAddress: Turn the domino around; it has the same dots. Circle two addends that make 10.

add-subtract-20-skill-04.target: I can use an addition fact to solve a related subtraction fact.

remedial.prompt: The picture shows 2 + 2 = 4. What is 4 − 2?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 2 red counters and 2 yellow counters.

standard.prompt: The whole bar is 15. One part is 8. What is the other part?

spec.alt: A bar for 15 split into two parts. One part is 8. The other part is unknown.

add-subtract-20-skill-04.misconception: Writing a subtraction fact that starts with a part (6 − 14 = 8).
add-subtract-20-skill-04.howToAddress: Use a part-part-whole mat: in subtraction the whole comes first.
commonErrors: counted back and included the starting number
forgot to go back past ten

equal-sign-skill-01.target: I can tell whether an equation is true or false by checking that both sides are the same amount.

remedial.prompt: The bars show 4 + 3 = 3 + 3. Write true or false.

spec.alt: Two bars. The top bar has parts 4 and 3. The bottom bar has parts 3 and 3.

steps: The bars are not the same length, so it is false.

standard.prompt: The bars show 3 + 4 = 5 + 2. Write true or false.

spec.alt: Two bars. The top bar has parts 3 and 4. The bottom bar has parts 5 and 2.

steps: The bars are the same length, so it is true.

equal-sign-skill-01.misconception: Thinking the equal sign means “the answer comes next,” so 7 = 7 or 5 = 2 + 3 looks wrong.
equal-sign-skill-01.howToAddress: Read = as “is the same as” and build each side with cubes.

equal-sign-skill-02.target: I can find the unknown number in an addition or subtraction equation.

remedial.prompt: The bar shows 4 + ___ = 5. What is the missing part?

spec.alt: A bar for 5 split into 4 and an unknown part.

standard.prompt: The bar shows 3 + ___ = 19. What is the missing part?

spec.alt: A bar for 19 split into 3 and an unknown part.

equal-sign-skill-02.howToAddress: Ask what number makes both sides the same; check by putting it in the blank.
commonErrors: copied a number from the equation

equal-sign-skill-03.target: I can find a number that makes both sides of an equation the same, such as 6 + 4 = 5 + ___.

remedial.prompt: The two bars are the same length. What number makes 5 + 5 = 4 + ___ true?

spec.alt: Two bars of the same length. The top bar has parts 5 and 5. The bottom bar has parts 4 and an unknown part.

standard.prompt: The two bars are the same length. What number makes 7 + 3 = 5 + ___ true?

spec.alt: Two bars of the same length. The top bar has parts 7 and 3. The bottom bar has parts 5 and an unknown part.

equal-sign-skill-03.misconception: Writing the total of the first side in the blank (6 + 4 = 5 + 10).
equal-sign-skill-03.howToAddress: Find the amount on the side you know, then ask what the other side still needs.
commonErrors: wrote the total of the other side

word-problems-20-skill-01.skill: Add To and Take From Stories
word-problems-20-skill-01.target: I can solve stories where some are added or taken away.

remedial.prompt: Sam had 9 cookies. Sam ate 3. The picture shows the story. How many cookies are left?

spec.alt: 9 counters. 3 of them are crossed out.

standard.prompt: Kai had 17 grapes. Kai ate 8. The picture shows the story. How many grapes are left?

spec.alt: 17 counters. 8 of them are crossed out.

word-problems-20-skill-01.misconception: Adding every pair of numbers in a story without thinking about what happened.
word-problems-20-skill-01.howToAddress: Act the story out: did the group get bigger or smaller?

word-problems-20-skill-02.skill: Put Together and Take Apart Stories
word-problems-20-skill-02.target: I can solve stories about two parts and a total.

remedial.prompt: There are 3 big beads and 6 small beads. The bar shows the story. How many beads in all?

spec.alt: A bar model with parts 3 and 6. The whole is unknown.

standard.prompt: There are 17 leaves. 8 are big. The rest are small. The bar shows the story. How many are small?

spec.alt: A bar model with whole 17 and parts 8 and unknown.

word-problems-20-skill-02.misconception: Adding the total and a part when a part is missing.
word-problems-20-skill-02.howToAddress: Draw a part-part-whole picture and label which number is the total.

word-problems-20-skill-03.target: I can solve stories that ask how many more or how many fewer.

remedial.prompt: Dan has 7 stickers. Kai has 3 stickers. The bars show both. How many more stickers does Dan have?

spec.alt: Two bars lined up. Dan's bar is 7 long. Kai's bar is 3 long.

steps: Line up the bars. The extra part is 7 − 3.

standard.prompt: Uma has 15 stickers. Cam has 12 stickers. The bars show both. How many more stickers does Uma have?

spec.alt: Two bars lined up. Uma's bar is 15 long. Cam's bar is 12 long.

steps: Line up the bars. The extra part is 15 − 12.

word-problems-20-skill-03.misconception: Adding because the word “more” appears in the question.
word-problems-20-skill-03.howToAddress: Line up the two groups and count the extra objects.

word-problems-20-skill-04.skill: Stories with a Missing Start or Change
word-problems-20-skill-04.target: I can solve stories where the start or the change is unknown.

remedial.prompt: Zoe had 3 stickers and got some more. Now Zoe has 7. The red counters show the start. How many stickers did Zoe get?

spec.alt: Ten frame with 3 red counters and 4 yellow counters.

steps: The yellow counters are the ones Zoe got.

standard.prompt: Liz had some cookies. Then Liz got 7 more. Now Liz has 13. How many cookies did Liz have at the start?

word-problems-20-skill-04.misconception: Using the last number in the story as the answer, or adding when the start is unknown.
word-problems-20-skill-04.howToAddress: Write an equation with a blank in the right place, then find the blank.

word-problems-20-skill-05.target: I can solve stories that add three numbers with a total up to 20.

remedial.prompt: Each circle shows a group of shells. How many shells are there in all?

spec.alt: Three circles of dots with 1, 3, and 2 dots.

standard.prompt: How many dots are in the three circles in all?

spec.alt: Three circles of dots with 4, 3, and 5 dots.

word-problems-20-skill-05.misconception: Adding only two of the three numbers.
word-problems-20-skill-05.howToAddress: Underline each number in the story and check that all three are added.

tens-ones-skill-01.target: I can make a ten from ten ones and tell how many tens and ones are in a group.

remedial.prompt: Make groups of ten. How many tens and how many ones are there?

spec.alt: 11 counters in rows of 10.

steps: Each full row of 10 is one ten.

standard.prompt: Make groups of ten. How many tens and how many ones are there?

spec.alt: 36 counters in rows of 10.

steps: Each full row of 10 is one ten.

tens-ones-skill-01.misconception: Counting a ten rod as one, not ten.
tens-ones-skill-01.howToAddress: Bundle ten straws and count the bundle as “ten.”
commonErrors: switched the tens and the ones

tens-ones-skill-02.target: I can show a number from 11 to 19 as one ten and some ones.

remedial.prompt: Write the number shown in the ten frames.

spec.alt: Two ten frames. The first is full. The second has 8 counters.

standard.prompt: What teen number do the ten frames show?

spec.alt: Two ten frames. The first is full. The second has 7 counters.

tens-ones-skill-02.misconception: Thinking 16 is 6 tens and 1 one, or writing sixteen as 61.
tens-ones-skill-02.howToAddress: Fill one ten frame and put the extra ones in a second frame.
commonErrors: switched the tens and the ones

tens-ones-skill-03.target: I can count by tens and tell how many tens are in 10, 20, 30, … 90.

remedial.prompt: Count the rods by tens. How many cubes are there?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 4 tens rods.

standard.prompt: Each rod is 10. What number is shown by the rods?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 6 tens rods.

tens-ones-skill-03.misconception: Thinking 50 is 5 ones, or counting by tens as 10, 20, 30, 31.

tens-ones-skill-04.skill: Tens and Ones in Two-Digit Numbers
tens-ones-skill-04.target: I can tell how many tens and ones are in a two-digit number and show it with blocks.

remedial.prompt: What number is shown by the blocks?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 4 tens rods and 3 ones cubes.

standard.prompt: What number is shown by the blocks?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 7 tens rods and 0 ones cubes.

tens-ones-skill-04.misconception: Mixing up the places (47 → 7 tens and 4 ones).
tens-ones-skill-04.howToAddress: Read the tens digit first, then build the rods and cubes to check.
commonErrors: switched the tens and the ones

compare-numbers-skill-01.target: I can tell which of two numbers is greater by comparing the tens first, then the ones.

remedial.prompt: The table shows the cubes each child has. Who has more cubes?

spec.alt: Table of blocks: Rosa has 2 tens and 5 ones. Nia has 1 ten and 1 one.

standard.prompt: The table shows the cubes each child has. Who has more cubes?

spec.alt: Table of blocks: Ian has 6 tens and 8 ones. Kim has 6 tens and 2 ones.

compare-numbers-skill-01.misconception: Comparing the ones digits first (29 is greater than 41 because 9 > 1).
compare-numbers-skill-01.howToAddress: Build both numbers with blocks; the number with more tens is greater.

compare-numbers-skill-02.target: I can write a comparison using the symbols >, =, and <.

remedial.prompt: The blocks show a number. Compare it to 32. Write >, <, or =: blocks ___ 32

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 5 tens rods and 8 ones cubes.

standard.prompt: The blocks show a number. Compare it to 76. Write >, <, or =: blocks ___ 76

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 7 tens rods and 4 ones cubes.

compare-numbers-skill-02.misconception: Pointing the symbol the wrong way.
compare-numbers-skill-02.howToAddress: The open side of the symbol faces the greater number.
commonErrors: pointed the symbol the wrong way
thought the numbers are the same

compare-numbers-skill-03.target: I can find numbers that make a comparison true and explain my thinking.

remedial.prompt: Write a number that is greater than 15 and less than 19.
steps: Any of these works, such as 16.

standard.prompt: Write a number that is greater than 75 and less than 80.
steps: Any of these works, such as 76.

compare-numbers-skill-03.misconception: Thinking a number with a bigger ones digit is always greater.
compare-numbers-skill-03.howToAddress: Check the tens digits first and use a number line to see which number comes later.
commonErrors: put them in the other order

add-subtract-100-skill-01.target: I can find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number without counting by ones.

remedial.prompt: The blocks show a number. What number is 10 more?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 5 tens rods and 9 ones cubes.

steps: The blocks show 59. Add one rod.

standard.prompt: The blocks show a number. What number is 10 more?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 4 tens rods and 2 ones cubes.

steps: The blocks show 42. Add one rod.

add-subtract-100-skill-01.misconception: Changing the ones digit instead of the tens digit (34 + 10 → 35).
add-subtract-100-skill-01.howToAddress: Add or take away one ten rod: only the tens digit changes.

add-subtract-100-skill-02.target: I can add tens to a two-digit number and subtract tens from tens.

remedial.prompt: The blocks show a number. Add 40 to it. What is the sum?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 4 tens rods and 0 ones cubes.

steps: The blocks show 40. Add 4 more tens.

standard.prompt: The blocks show a number. Add 10 to it. What is the sum?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 1 ten rods and 1 one cubes.

steps: The blocks show 11. Add 1 more ten.

add-subtract-100-skill-02.misconception: Adding the tens to the ones (40 + 23 → 27), or writing 50 − 20 = 3.
add-subtract-100-skill-02.howToAddress: Think in tens: 5 tens − 2 tens = 3 tens, which is 30.
commonErrors: made a mistake with the tens

add-subtract-100-skill-03.skill: Adding a Two-Digit and a One-Digit Number
add-subtract-100-skill-03.target: I can add a one-digit number to a two-digit number when no new ten is made.

remedial.prompt: The blocks show a number. Add 5 more ones. What is the sum?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 4 tens rods and 3 ones cubes.

standard.prompt: The blocks show a number. Add 2 more ones. What is the sum?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 6 tens rods and 5 ones cubes.

add-subtract-100-skill-03.misconception: Adding the one-digit number to the tens (32 + 5 → 82).
add-subtract-100-skill-03.howToAddress: Add ones to ones and keep the tens.
commonErrors: added the ones to the tens

add-subtract-100-skill-04.target: I can add a one-digit number to a two-digit number when the ones make a new ten.

remedial.prompt: The blocks show a number. Add 2 ones. Make a new ten if you can. What is the sum?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 4 tens rods and 8 ones cubes.

steps: The blocks show 48. 8 ones + 2 ones = 10 ones = 1 ten and 0 ones.

standard.prompt: The blocks show a number. Add 8 ones. Make a new ten if you can. What is the sum?

spec.alt: Base-ten blocks: 1 ten rods and 9 ones cubes.

steps: The blocks show 19. 9 ones + 8 ones = 17 ones = 1 ten and 7 ones.

add-subtract-100-skill-04.misconception: Writing the ones sum as a digit (38 + 5 → 313).
add-subtract-100-skill-04.howToAddress: Fill the ten first: 38 + 2 = 40, then add the 3 left.
commonErrors: did not make a new ten
wrote the ones sum as two digits
counted on and included the first number

add-subtract-100-skill-05.target: I can add two two-digit numbers within 100 by adding tens and tens and ones and ones.

remedial.prompt: The table shows two numbers as tens and ones. What is the sum of the two numbers?

spec.alt: Table: first number 3 tens and 7 ones; second number 3 tens and 2 ones.

standard.prompt: The table shows two numbers as tens and ones. What is the sum of the two numbers?

spec.alt: Table: first number 3 tens and 7 ones; second number 3 tens and 1 one.

add-subtract-100-skill-05.misconception: Adding a tens digit to a ones digit.
add-subtract-100-skill-05.howToAddress: Draw tens as lines and ones as dots; add each kind separately.

measuring-length-skill-01.target: I can compare two lengths and put three objects in order from shortest to longest.

remedial.prompt: Put the objects in order from shortest to longest.

spec.alt: Objects lined up at the left: Yarn 3 units long, Rope 5 units long, Ruler 10 units long.

steps: The order is Yarn, Rope, Ruler.

standard.prompt: Which object is longest?

spec.alt: Objects lined up at the left: Brush 6 units long, Yarn 7 units long, Spoon 9 units long.

steps: The ends are lined up at the left, so compare the right ends.

measuring-length-skill-01.misconception: Comparing objects that do not start at the same line.
measuring-length-skill-01.howToAddress: Line up the ends before comparing.
commonErrors: chose the wrong end of the order
put them in the opposite order

measuring-length-skill-02.target: I can use a third object to compare two lengths.

remedial.prompt: The couch is longer than the yarn. The yarn is longer than the chair. Is the couch longer or shorter than the chair?
steps: The couch is longer than the yarn, and the yarn is longer than the chair.
So the couch is longer than the chair.

standard.prompt: A bus is shorter than the train. The bus is longer than the van. Which is longer, the train or the van?
steps: The train is longer than the bus, and the bus is longer than the van.
So the train is longer than the van.

measuring-length-skill-02.misconception: Thinking a comparison cannot be made without putting the two objects side by side.
measuring-length-skill-02.howToAddress: If the rug is longer than the string and the string is longer than the desk, the rug is longer than the desk.
commonErrors: did not use the middle object to compare

measuring-length-skill-03.target: I can measure a length by counting same-size units laid end to end.

remedial.prompt: The paper clips are lined up end to end. How long is the stick?

spec.alt: A stick with 3 paper clips laid end to end under it, with no gaps or overlaps.

steps: Count the paper clips under the stick.
The stick is 3 paper clips long.

standard.prompt: The paper clips are lined up end to end. How long is the pencil?

spec.alt: A pencil with 5 paper clips laid end to end under it, with no gaps or overlaps.

steps: Count the paper clips under the pencil.
The pencil is 5 paper clips long.

measuring-length-skill-03.misconception: Counting the spaces or lines instead of the units.
measuring-length-skill-03.howToAddress: Count each cube or paper clip as you touch it.
commonErrors: counted the lines, not the units

measuring-length-skill-04.target: I can tell when a measurement is wrong because of gaps, overlaps, or units of different sizes.

remedial.prompt: Dev measured the yarn with gaps and got 5 cubes. Count the squares to measure the right way. How long is the yarn?

spec.alt: A yarn 6 units long on a grid of same-size squares.

steps: Count each square under the object with no gaps.

standard.prompt: Tom measured the brush with gaps and got 8 cubes. Count the squares to measure the right way. How long is the brush?

spec.alt: A brush 10 units long on a grid of same-size squares.

steps: Count each square under the object with no gaps.

measuring-length-skill-04.misconception: Leaving gaps or overlaps, or mixing big and small units.
measuring-length-skill-04.howToAddress: Check that units touch end to end and are all the same size.

telling-time-skill-01.target: I can tell and write time to the hour on analog and digital clocks.

remedial.prompt: What time does the clock show? Write it like a digital clock.

spec.alt: Analog clock. The short hour hand points to the 3. The long minute hand points to the 12.

steps: The short hand points to 3. The long hand points to 12.

standard.prompt: Write the time shown on the clock.

spec.alt: Analog clock. The short hour hand points to the 11. The long minute hand points to the 12.

steps: The short hand points to 11. The long hand points to 12.

telling-time-skill-01.misconception: Mixing up the hour hand and the minute hand.
telling-time-skill-01.howToAddress: The short hand tells the hour; the long hand points to 12 at o'clock.
commonErrors: mixed up o'clock and half past
mixed up the hour hand and the minute hand

telling-time-skill-02.target: I can tell and write time to the half hour on analog and digital clocks.

remedial.prompt: Write the time shown on the clock.

spec.alt: Analog clock. The short hour hand points halfway between the 5 and the 6. The long minute hand points to the 6.

steps: The hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is 5. The minute hand points to 6, which means 30 minutes.

standard.prompt: What time does the clock show? Write it like a digital clock.

spec.alt: Analog clock. The short hour hand points halfway between the 1 and the 2. The long minute hand points to the 6.

steps: The hour hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is 1. The minute hand points to 6, which means 30 minutes.

telling-time-skill-02.misconception: Reading the next hour at half past (the hour hand is past 3, so it says 4:30).
telling-time-skill-02.howToAddress: At half past, the hour hand is halfway between two numbers; read the number it has passed.
commonErrors: mixed up o'clock and half past
read the minute hand number as minutes

telling-time-skill-03.target: I can match analog and digital times and tell what time it will be one hour or half an hour later.

remedial.prompt: The clock shows the time the game starts. The game lasts 1 hour. What time does it end? Write it like a digital clock.

spec.alt: Analog clock. The short hour hand points to the 4. The long minute hand points to the 12.

standard.prompt: The clock shows the time the game starts. The game lasts 1 hour. What time does it end? Write it like a digital clock.

spec.alt: Analog clock. The short hour hand points to the 7. The long minute hand points to the 12.

telling-time-skill-03.howToAddress: Half past means 30 minutes; the long hand points to 6.
commonErrors: mixed up o'clock and half past

data-skill-01.target: I can sort objects into up to three groups and use tally marks to show how many.

remedial.prompt: How many dogs do the tally marks show?

spec.alt: Tally chart with one row, Dogs, showing 4 tally marks in bundles of five.

steps: A bundle of 4 marks crossed by a slash is 5. Count by fives, then count on by ones.

standard.prompt: Count the tally marks for Votes. What number do they show?

spec.alt: Tally chart with one row, Votes, showing 10 tally marks in bundles of five.

steps: A bundle of 4 marks crossed by a slash is 5. Count by fives, then count on by ones.

data-skill-01.misconception: Counting each bundle of five tally marks as one.
data-skill-01.howToAddress: Count tally bundles by fives, then count on by ones.

data-skill-02.target: I can read how many are in each category of a picture graph, tally chart, or table.

remedial.prompt: The tally chart shows favorite fruit. What number goes with Banana?

spec.alt: Tally chart titled Favorite Fruit. Apple 3, Banana 2, Grape 5.

standard.prompt: Look at the tally chart. How many children chose Pizza?

spec.alt: Tally chart titled Lunch Choice. Pizza 7, Tacos 14, Soup 5.

data-skill-02.misconception: Reading the wrong row or counting the label.
data-skill-02.howToAddress: Point to the category name, then slide across the row.

data-skill-03.target: I can find the total and tell how many more or fewer are in one category than another.

remedial.prompt: How many children are shown in the picture graph in all?

spec.alt: Picture graph titled Recess Games. Each star stands for 1. Soccer 6, Tag 8, Swings 5.

standard.prompt: Use the tally chart. How many are Grape or Apple? Add them.

spec.alt: Tally chart titled Favorite Fruit. Apple 4, Banana 6, Grape 14.

data-skill-03.misconception: Adding when the question asks how many more.
data-skill-03.howToAddress: Find the two numbers first, then decide: in all means add; how many more means compare.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.target: I can tell which attributes make a shape what it is (closed, number of sides and corners) and which do not (color, size, position).

remedial.prompt: Count the corners of the shape. How many?

spec.alt: One pink triangle.

steps: Count each corner once. Touch them as you count.

standard.prompt: Count the sides of the shape. How many?

spec.alt: One yellow triangle, turned.

steps: Count each side once. Touch them as you count.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.misconception: Thinking a turned square is not a square, or that color or size changes a shape's name.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.howToAddress: Turn and resize paper shapes; count sides and corners again.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.target: I can name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and rectangular prisms.

remedial.prompt: Name this shape.

spec.alt: A blue square.

steps: Count the sides and corners, and look for curves.

standard.prompt: Name this shape.

spec.alt: A blue triangle, turned.

steps: Count the sides and corners, and look for curves.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.misconception: Calling every four-sided shape a square, or calling a cylinder a circle.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.howToAddress: Count sides and corners; for solids, look for flat faces and curved surfaces.
commonErrors: named it by how it looks

shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.target: I can put shapes together to make new shapes and tell how many shapes I used.

remedial.prompt: The square is made of triangles. How many triangles are used?

spec.alt: A square made of 2 triangles, with each piece outlined.

standard.prompt: The trapezoid is made of triangles. How many triangles are used?

spec.alt: A trapezoid made of 3 triangles, with each piece outlined.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.misconception: Thinking a new shape cannot be made from smaller pieces, or counting outlines instead of pieces.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.howToAddress: Use pattern blocks to cover a shape and count the pieces.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.target: I can split circles and rectangles into 2 or 4 equal shares and name halves, fourths, and quarters.

remedial.prompt: What are the parts called? Write halves, fourths, or not equal shares.

spec.alt: A square cut into 2 equal parts.

steps: Check that the parts are the same size, then count them.
There are 2 equal parts, so: halves.

standard.prompt: What are the parts called? Write halves, fourths, or not equal shares.

spec.alt: A square cut into 2 unequal parts.

steps: Check that the parts are the same size, then count them.
There are 2 unequal parts, so: not equal shares.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.misconception: Calling unequal parts halves or fourths.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.howToAddress: Fold paper shapes so the parts match exactly.
commonErrors: thought one share is the whole

shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.target: I can describe a whole as two halves or four fourths and explain that more equal shares are smaller shares.

remedial.prompt: A waffle is cut into fourths. Jay eats 2 of the shares. How many shares are left?

standard.prompt: A cake is cut into fourths. Kai eats 1 of the shares. How many shares are left?

shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.misconception: Thinking a fourth is bigger than a half because 4 is bigger than 2.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.howToAddress: Cut two same-size paper strips into halves and fourths and compare the pieces.
